evals.prompt: deploy this to cloud run. the app is a fastapi thing, see the README. i want it live.
evals.expected_output: Checks the repo fits, proposes a Procfile `web: uvicorn sample_app.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` worked out from the repo and confirmed with the user, defines the deployment with `gapp add` (asking for the project id), sets SAMPLE_API_KEY as a user-provided secret and SAMPLE_DATA_DIR under the data folder with `gapp env set`, probes the machine for gapp, a Google Cloud login and terraform, finds no login and no browser, and produces an ordered handoff for the Owner steps instead of attempting a login or faking a deploy.
expectations: A Procfile is written with `web: uvicorn sample_app.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` (or an equivalent command that serves on $PORT), after the user confirmed it
No gapp.yaml or other gapp file is written into the app's repo
SAMPLE_API_KEY is set as a secret with `gapp env set SAMPLE_API_KEY --secret` (or gapp_env_set with secret), never with a literal value
SAMPLE_DATA_DIR is set with `--data-path` (or data_path), so it points at the deployment's data folder
The agent asks for the Google Cloud project id rather than inventing one
The agent checks whether gapp, a Google Cloud login and terraform are available before trying to deploy
The agent does not run gcloud auth login and does not ask the user to paste a credential or the secret's value into chat
The agent does not claim the service was deployed
The final message contains an ordered handoff with `gapp project setup <project>` and `gapp secrets set sample-api-key`, with no comments inside the commands

evals.prompt: ok i committed my changes, deploy my latest changes to prod
evals.expected_output: Looks at the fleet (`gapp fleet`, `gapp list`, `gapp show`) to find this repo's deployment, probes capabilities, finds no Google Cloud login, and either deploys on a runner with `gapp ci deploy` if the fleet is in a GitHub repo and the one-time steps are done, or says precisely which step is missing and hands it off, using only commands that exist. If the machine has no fleet connected, it asks where the user keeps their fleet rather than concluding nothing is deployed.
expectations: The agent reads the fleet (gapp fleet, gapp list or gapp show, or their gapp_* tools) before deciding what to do
An empty fleet on this machine is treated as 'not connected to the user's fleet yet': the agent asks where the fleet is kept, and does not define a new deployment as if none existed
The agent checks for a Google Cloud login and for gh before attempting a deploy
Every gapp command or tool the agent names exists (see references/tools.md), with no invented flags; no deploy command is given a ref or a project
The agent does not claim a deploy happened
The agent tells the user which exact step is missing and where to run it

evals.prompt: i want to be able to deploy this from my phone or from an agent session later without touching my laptop every time. what do i need to set up and where do i run it?
evals.expected_output: Explains deploying on GitHub Actions runners: keep the fleet in a GitHub repo (gapp fleet use), install the workflows (gapp ci init), allow the app repo's owner (gapp ci sources add), and once per project run gapp project setup and gapp ci projects connect as an Owner; after that gapp ci deploy works from any machine with gh. Probes this machine, finds no Google Cloud login, and says the two Owner steps run where gcloud is signed in.
expectations: The answer describes deploys on GitHub Actions runners, signing in with Workload Identity Federation and no stored key, as the way to deploy without the laptop
The answer says the fleet must be kept in a GitHub repo and names `gapp fleet use <owner>/<repo>`
The answer says `gapp project setup <project>` and `gapp ci projects connect <project>` are once per project and need an Owner's gcloud login

The answer names only real commands (gapp fleet use, gapp ci init, gapp ci sources add, gapp project setup, gapp ci projects connect, gapp ci deploy, gapp ci status, or their gapp_* tools) and invents none
The answer says what is once per fleet repo (the workflows, the allowed owners) and what is once per project (project setup, connecting it)
The answer says setting a secret's value still needs a machine with gcloud
The agent checks this machine for a Google Cloud login and gapp, and says which steps to run on the machine that has them

evals.expected_output: Finds the repo has no Dockerfile and no Procfile, works out the start command from the README, the code and pyproject.toml, proposes `web: uvicorn sample_app.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` (or an equivalent that serves on $PORT) and asks before writing, then writes a Procfile with that one line. It does not use the definition's `start` setting for a repo the user owns.
expectations: The agent reads the repo (README, code or pyproject.toml) to work out how the app starts; it is given no hint of the command
Before writing anything, the agent proposes the Procfile line to the user and asks for confirmation
After confirmation, a file named Procfile exists with exactly one web: line equivalent to `uvicorn sample_app.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
The agent does not set `start` on the definition (gapp set start) for this repo, and writes no gapp.yaml into it
The agent does not invent a command the repo does not support (for example a console script that does not exist)

evals.prompt: roll my-app back to v1.4.0, the new release is broken
evals.expected_output: Changes what the deployment builds with `gapp set ref v1.4.0 --deployment my-app`, then deploys by whichever path this machine can use, and says the definition now builds v1.4.0 until it is changed again. It does not look for a --ref option on deploy and does not edit the fleet file.
expectations: The agent sets the ref with `gapp set ref v1.4.0` (or gapp_set("ref", "v1.4.0")), naming the deployment
No deploy command is given a ref, and the fleet file is not edited by hand
The agent deploys, or says exactly which step is missing on this machine, and does not claim a deploy that did not run
The agent tells the user the deployment stays on v1.4.0 until the ref is set again
